call_memory.speaker: MANAGEMENT
call_memory.statement: The Middle East crisis has disrupted sulfur supply chains, affecting availability and prices globally.

lab.quote: And now, it's again back to normal as I mentioned, but for maybe 15 days, we ran at perhaps 60% capacity.

call_memory.speaker: MANAGEMENT
call_memory.statement: Roha plant operated at 60% capacity for 15 days in March due to raw material availability challenges.

lab.quote: The first half of the year, we lost a lot of production because of disruption in supply of the boron ore from our main supplier in Turkey.

call_memory.quote: The first half of the year, we lost a lot of production because of disruption in supply of the boron ore from our main supplier in Turkey.
call_memory.speaker: MANAGEMENT
call_memory.statement: Boron business faced production loss in H1 FY26 due to supply disruption of boron ore from Turkey.

lab.quote: The overall year, we ended at INR 582 crores, which is one of the highest top lines in the company.

call_memory.quote: The overall year, we ended at INR 582 crores, which is one of the highest top lines in the company.
call_memory.speaker: MANAGEMENT
call_memory.statement: The company ended FY26 with a top line of INR 582 crores.

lab.quote: First of all, for the Boron business, which went from a situation of where we were getting credit and picking up material from stocks in India to a position where we had to pay advance and got material 90 days to 120 days after paying the advance.

call_memory.quote: First of all, for the Boron business, which went from a situation of where we were getting credit and picking up material from stocks in India to a position where we had to pay advance and got material 90 days to 120 days after paying the advance.
call_memory.speaker: MANAGEMENT
call_memory.statement: Working capital intensity increased due to boron business shifting to advance payment terms and higher sulfur prices.

lab.quote: But all I can say is that we expect it to be better than it was in FY25-26.

call_memory.quote: But all I can say is that we expect it to be better than it was in FY25-26.
call_memory.speaker: MANAGEMENT
call_memory.statement: Management expects speciality chemical business performance to be better in FY27 than in FY26.

lab.quote: Both plants are very similar. ... Almost 350 tons per day around that for Dahej as well.

call_memory.quote: Both plants are very similar. ... Almost 350 tons per day around that for Dahej as well.
call_memory.speaker: MANAGEMENT
call_memory.statement: Both Dahej and Roha plants have a sulfuric acid capacity of approximately 350 tons per day each.

call_points.text: Sulfur availability and pricing remain volatile due to disruptions around the Gulf of Hormuz.
Dahej plant operated normally while Roha faced temporary slowdowns due to raw material logistics.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company had received Differential Duty demand of Rs. 14.33 crores (on Import of crude/un-refined Sulphur during the period 2004-2005 to 2008-2009, provisionally assessed then), at concessional rate of Basic Customs Duty in term of Entry at Sr. No. 60 of Notification No. 21/2002- Cus dated March 01, 2002 which granted concessional rate of basic customs duty on the import of “Crude or unrefined Sulphur” falling under Chapter Sub-heading No. 2503 00 of Customs Tariff). The Company had filed an Appeal before CESTAT being Appeal No. C/89904/2018 – DB dated January 02, 2019 (against the Order dated February 07, 2018 of the Commissioner (Appeals), Mumbai) and deposited an amount of Rs.1.43 crores (being the 10% of the alleged demand of differential duty of ` 14.33 crores), as a condition precedent for the Appeal before the CESTAT. The Appeal is pending at CESTAT, Mumbai, and will come up for hearing in course of time. Based on the legal advice the Company is confident to successfully succeed in the appeal.
tax_litigation.status: Pending at CESTAT for Adjudication

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company had imported Rock Phosphate (for the manufacture of Fertilizer viz. Single Superphosphate) and the Bill of Entry for the consignments of Rock Phosphate imported during the period 2005-2006 to 2007-2008, were provisionally assessed and goods were allowed to be cleared with “Nil” Special additional Duty (SAD for short) falling under Chapter heading, Sub-heading or tariff item “31 or any other chapter” of the first Schedule of Customs Tariff. Subsequently, the Department raised an alleged demand of ` 1.21 crores on account of the enhancement of declared value (Invoice value on which duty was assessed provisionally) and denial of “Nil” (SAD) under Notification- 20/2006-Cus dated March 01, 2006 on the alleged ground that the Company had allegedly failed to submit the relevant documents which could prove that the imported Rock Phosphate was used for the manufacturing of “fertilizer”. The Company had filed an Appeal before CESTAT being Appeal No. C/89910/2018 – DB dated January 02, 2019 (against the Order dated February 07, 2018 of the Commissioner (Appeals), Mumbai.)and deposited an amount of Rs. 12.16 lakhs being the 10% of the alleged demand of Rs. 1.21 crores. The Appeal is pending at CESTAT, Mumbai and will come up for hearing in course of time. Based on the legal advice the Company is confident to successfully succeed in the appeal.
tax_litigation.status: Pending at CESTAT for Adjudication

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company had received Differential Duty demand of Rs. 14.33 crores (on Import of crude/un-refined Sulphur during the period 2004-2005 to 2008-2009, provisionally assessed then), at concessional rate of Basic Customs Duty in term of Entry at Sr. No. 60 of Notification No. 21/2002- Cus dated March 01, 2002 which granted concessional rate of basic customs duty on the import of “Crude or unrefined Sulphur” falling under Chapter Sub-heading No. 2503 00 of Customs Tariff). The Company had filed an Appeal before CESTAT being Appeal No. C/89904/2018 – DB dated January 02, 2019 (against the Order dated February 07, 2018 of the Commissioner (Appeals), Mumbai) and deposited an amount of Rs.1.43 crores (being the 10% of the alleged demand of differential duty of ` 14.33 crores), as a condition precedent for the Appeal before the CESTAT. The Appeal is pending at CESTAT, Mumbai, and will come up for hearing in course of time. Based on the legal advice the Company is confident to successfully succeed in the appeal.
tax_litigation.status: Pending at CESTAT for Adjudication

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company had imported Rock Phosphate (for the manufacture of Fertilizer viz. Single Superphosphate) and the Bill of Entry for the consignments of Rock Phosphate imported during the period 2005-2006 to 2007-2008, were provisionally assessed and goods were allowed to be cleared with “Nil” Special additional Duty (SAD for short) falling under Chapter heading, Sub-heading or tariff item “31 or any other chapter” of the first Schedule of Customs Tariff. Subsequently, the Department raised an alleged demand of ` 1.21 crores on account of the enhancement of declared value (Invoice value on which duty was assessed provisionally) and denial of “Nil” (SAD) under Notification- 20/2006-Cus dated March 01, 2006 on the alleged ground that the Company had allegedly failed to submit the relevant documents which could prove that the imported Rock Phosphate was used for the manufacturing of “fertilizer”. The Company had filed an Appeal before CESTAT being Appeal No. C/89910/2018 – DB dated January 02, 2019 (against the Order dated February 07, 2018 of the Commissioner (Appeals), Mumbai.)and deposited an amount of Rs. 12.16 lakhs being the 10% of the alleged demand of Rs. 1.21 crores. The Appeal is pending at CESTAT, Mumbai and will come up for hearing in course of time. Based on the legal advice the Company is confident to successfully succeed in the appeal.
tax_litigation.status: Pending at CESTAT for Adjudication

timeline.summary: CRISIL reaffirmed DMCC Specialty Chemicals' BBB+/Stable rating on bank facilities of ₹139.51 Cr and fixed deposits of ₹20 Cr.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹177.64 Cr (+41.9% YoY), net profit ₹7.65 Cr (+18.2% YoY).
DMCC Speciality Chemicals reported Q4FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹177.64 Cr and net profit of ₹7.65 Cr.
Pallavi Satish, Director, signed the audio recording submission for Q4FY26 earnings conference call on May 19, 2026.
DMCC Specialty Chemicals received an appeal order from the Additional Commissioner (Appeals Raigad) concerning an input tax credit demand of ₹1.06 Cr.
DMCC Specialty Chemicals reported Q4FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹177.64 Cr and PAT of ₹7.65 Cr during its earnings call on May 19, 2026.
